meta.tagline: A castle on the Neckar, a bridge and the capital of romanticism

pills: An old town that escaped the war almost untouched

overview.title: Welcome to Heidelberg
overview.intro: Heidelberg is called the city of poets, and you understand why at first glance: the half-ruined red sandstone castle watches the old town from its slope, the Neckar slides beneath the arches of the stone bridge, and on the far bank the Philosophers' Way winds through the vineyards. Goethe lost his heart here; Twain gave it pages. Germany's oldest university keeps the city forever young: student taverns, bicycles and riverside picnics. Romance here is not scenery — it is daily life.

local_word.definition: The untranslatable German word: the sum of warmth, comfort and belonging. The moment you raise a beer by candlelight at a wooden tavern table — that feeling is Gemütlichkeit.

rules.title: See the town from the castle, and the castle from the town
rules.description: The castle is both stage and box seat: first go up by Bergbahn or the stairs and look over the town from the terrace, then watch the castle itself from the Philosophers' Way. The two angles complete each other — either alone is half the picture.

rules.title: Fall in with the student city's rhythm
rules.description: Heidelberg's soul lives at the university: the taverns have been full of student tables for centuries, and the Karzer's walls are covered with old offenders' scribbles. Choose the student classics over the tourist menu — cheaper and truer.

rules.title: Remember to leave the main street
rules.description: The Hauptstraße is one of Europe's longest pedestrian streets, but Heidelberg's secrets hide in its side lanes: quiet courtyards, small squares, baroque doorways. Make the main street your spine and explore the ribs.

quick_facts.label: Getting around
quick_facts.sub: The old town walks end to end

tip.label: The Heidelberg philosophy
tip.text: This city is planned around sunset: the evening light turns the castle's sandstone to embers. Whatever you do by day, at that hour be on the bridge or the Philosophers' Way.

transport.title: Getting Around
transport.intro: The old town is walked; tram and bus tie in the station, and the funicular solves the castle and the summit.

items.title: Arriving from Frankfurt
items.description: From Frankfurt airport, a train or direct shuttle reaches Heidelberg in about an hour. The station sits away from the old town — take the tram to Bismarckplatz, where the wandering begins.

items.title: The tram and bus network
items.description: The VRN network wraps the city: Bismarckplatz is the main knot, and buses run into the old town. A day ticket is practical for the station-centre-castle triangle.

items.title: The Bergbahn — a two-stage funicular
items.description: The funicular from Kornmarkt climbs first to the castle, then in century-old wooden carriages to the Königstuhl summit: the lower line is modern, the upper pure 1907 nostalgia. The combined ticket includes castle admission.

items.title: The old town on foot
items.description: The Hauptstraße's 1.6 kilometres and its side lanes walk end to end; the steep stair to the castle (Burgweg) is a 15-minute climb. Comfortable soles are essential for the cobbles.

items.title: The Neckar banks by bike
items.description: The riverside cycle paths are flat and the bridges link both banks: the route from the Neckarwiese lawns to the neighbouring towns is a sunny day's best plan.

callout.label: Funicular tip
callout.text: Ride all the way to Königstuhl: most people get off at the castle stop, and the wooden-carriage upper line is nearly empty. On a clear day the Rhine plain shows all the way to the Vosges — get off at the castle on the way down and collect both views on one ticket.

stay.title: Where to Stay
stay.intro: In Heidelberg it's a question of riverbank and castle distance: stone-lane romance, or riverside calm?

local_word.definition: The old town: the historic core of baroque façades and stone lanes that came through the war almost untouched. In Heidelberg, saying 'I'm staying in the Altstadt' means waking up inside the city's fairytale set.

items.name: Altstadt (the Old Town)
items.description: Stone lanes at the castle's foot: taverns, squares and the bridge two steps away. Student life is lively at night — the price of the romance is some noise, the reward a castle view from your window.

items.name: Neuenheim
items.description: A calm quarter of art nouveau façades on the far bank: the start of the Philosophers' Way, the Neckarwiese lawns and neighbourhood cafés. Five minutes to the Altstadt over the bridge — a balance of quiet and view.

items.name: Weststadt
items.description: A settled quarter of Gründerzeit apartment houses: near the station, warm cafés, friendly prices. Real Heidelberg daily life off the tourist route.

items.name: Bergheim
items.description: The modern belt between Bismarckplatz and the station: hotels, shopping and the crossing of every tram. Little character, flawless access — the efficient base for a short visit.

items.name: Handschuhsheim
items.description: The old village core to the north: half-timbered houses, vineyard slopes and the little Tiefburg castle. Ten minutes to the centre by tram — for village calm with city access.

best_time.title: When to Go
best_time.intro: Heidelberg is photogenic in every season: vineyards green in spring, castle illuminations in summer, and in December the squares become one long Christmas market.

items.label: Spring
items.name: Philosophers' Season
items.subtitle: Spring · Flowering slopes, the river wakes
items.description: The gardens of the Philosophers' Way bloom, the Neckarwiese greets its first picnickers, the terraces go up. The city is at its freshest — the golden balance for walking and photography.

callout.label: April tip
callout.text: In late April the almond and cherry blossom opens early in the Philosophers' Way's microclimate: walk it in morning light, and the castle appears from the far slope framed in pink.

items.label: Summer
items.name: Castle Lights
items.subtitle: Summer · Castle illuminations, river evenings
items.description: The summer evenings are long: the Neckarwiese turns into a beach, and on certain Saturdays the castle illumination and fireworks are watched from the bridge. The crowds peak at noon — morning and evening are yours.

callout.label: Summer tip
callout.text: On Schlossbeleuchtung nights — one Saturday each in June, July and September — the bridge and banks fill early: claim your spot on the Neuenheim shore in the late afternoon and watch the fireworks burst over the castle with their reflection in the river.

items.label: Autumn
items.name: The Golden Valley
items.subtitle: Autumn · Copper forests, new wine
items.description: The Odenwald forests turn copper, the vineyard harvest begins, and the taverns open the season of new wine (Neuer Wein) with onion tart. The university term starts — the city grows young again.

callout.label: October tip
callout.text: In October ride up the Königstuhl and look down on the colouring valley; on the way down, try new wine + Zwiebelkuchen in Handschuhsheim's vineyard taverns — autumn's official menu.

items.label: Winter
items.name: A Christmas Tale
items.subtitle: Winter · Christmas markets square by square
items.description: In December the old town's squares link into a chain of Christmas markets; on Karlsplatz an ice rink rises with a castle view. January and February are quiet and misty — and in that mist the castle is at its most mysterious.

callout.label: December tip
callout.text: Do the Christmas market on a weekday evening and end the route at Kornmarkt: the lit castle directly above you, mulled wine in hand — the postcard moment of a Heidelberg winter.

eat.title: What to Eat
eat.intro: Heidelberg's cooking was written in its student taverns: hearty Baden-Palatinate classics, regional wines and a 160-year-old chocolate kiss.

local_word.definition: The 'student's kiss': a chocolate invented in 1863 by a confectioner for students who could not openly court the chaperoned young ladies. Still sold in its elegant box at the same shop — the city's sweetest piece of history.

items.name: Schnitzel — tavern-sized
items.description: A schnitzel overflowing the plate with potato salad alongside: the unchanging classic of the student taverns. The Jäger version (mushroom sauce) is autumn's favourite.
items.tag: At a student tavern · bigger than the plate

items.name: Käsespätzle and Maultaschen
items.description: Southern Germany's answer to pasta: cheese spätzle with fried onions, and Maultaschen, the 'German ravioli'. Both filling, both friends of beer.

items.name: Palatinate and Baden wines
items.description: Germany's sunniest wine regions are two steps away: local glasses from Riesling to Spätburgunder at tavern prices. Order a 'Schoppen' (the big glass) — it's the regional tradition.

items.name: A Studentenkuss break
items.description: A chocolate kiss + filter coffee at the historic confectioner's: you taste a 160-year-old flirtation as you listen. The box is Heidelberg's most elegant gift.
items.tag: At the historic confectioner's · gift box

items.name: Brezel and bakery culture
items.description: A warm pretzel from the morning bakery with butter: the German ritual for starting the day. At noon, the belegte Brötchen (filled rolls) at the bakery counters are the budget meal.
items.tag: Morning ritual · warm from the oven

items.name: Tavern beer from the cask
items.description: In the centuries-old student taverns the local beer comes from the cask, and the walls are covered in old sabre marks and crests. Sharing the long wooden table with strangers isn't a rule — it's the pleasure.
items.tag: In a historic tavern · from the cask

callout.label: The tavern rule
callout.text: Skip the Hauptstraße's shop-window restaurants for the historic taverns two lanes in: half the price, twice the story. Enter the door with a student crest and a fencing sabre on the wall — you're in the right place.

hidden_gems.title: Hidden Corners
hidden_gems.intro: Everyone sees the castle; these six are Heidelberg's backstage.

items.name: The Studentenkarzer
items.description: The university's student jail, used until 1914: misbehaving students filled the walls with silhouette portraits and verses. Not a prison but a monument to youth — Heidelberg's oddest, most lovable museum.

items.name: The Philosophenweg
items.description: The path winding through vineyards on the far slope: castle, bridge and old town give their best angle from here. Its microclimate even grows figs — go up at sunset and sit long on one of the benches.

items.rarity: A stone amphitheatre in the forest
items.name: The Thingstätte
items.description: The huge open-air amphitheatre on the Heiligenberg, with medieval monastery ruins beside it: a strange, powerful place in the forest's silence. Reached by the path continuing from the Philosophers' Way.

items.rarity: The palace of the giant barrel
items.name: The Great Tun and the Pharmacy Museum
items.description: The 220,000-litre wine barrel in the castle cellar and the German Pharmacy Museum are the two surprises most visitors skip: you climb stairs onto the barrel's top, and the museum smells of alchemy.

items.name: The Neckarwiese
items.description: The long strip of lawn on the Neuenheim bank: the city's beach, picnic ground and sunset box. The castle silhouette across the water — barbecue smoke and student guitars included.

items.name: The Bridge Monkey and the Karl Theodor Bridge
items.description: The bronze monkey at the Alte Brücke's gate holds up a mirror: touching it promises a return to the city, touching its fingers promises fortune. And the bridge itself, in morning mist, gives the city's best photograph.

callout.label: Morning tip
callout.text: Go to the Alte Brücke just after sunrise: the bridge empty, mist on the river, the castle pink in first light. The same frame becomes a selfie stage for tour groups by noon — take your postcard early.

traps.title: Tourist Traps
traps.intro: Heidelberg is an honest town; its traps are small, hidden inside the day-trippers' routine.

items.name: Misreading the castle ticket
items.description: The courtyard and terraces are open on the normal ticket, but the interiors open only with a timed guided tour; whoever doesn't know this sulks at the door.
items.instead: Courtyard + barrel + pharmacy museum satisfies most visitors; if you want the interiors, book the tour slot at the entrance right away. The Bergbahn combined ticket already includes castle admission.

items.name: Eating in the Hauptstraße's shop window
items.description: The main street's photo menus sell average cooking at tourist prices; the same schnitzel two lanes in is both better and cheaper.
items.instead: Choose the side-lane taverns and the university quarter; at lunch, the boards that say Mittagstisch (dish of the day) are the budget's friend.

items.name: Getting caught in the midday tour wave
items.description: The day-trip coaches fill the castle and bridge between 11 and 4: queues, crowds and shadeless waiting.
items.instead: Do the castle at opening or after 4 pm; give midday to Neuenheim, the museums and a tavern break. The light is more beautiful in the late afternoon anyway.

items.name: Driving into the old town
items.description: The Altstadt is largely pedestrianised, parking scarce and the garages expensive; a wrong entry introduces you to a fine.
items.instead: Leave the car in the ring garages (marked P) or don't bring one at all: train + tram + feet handle everything in this town.

callout.label: Golden rule
callout.text: Heidelberg's crowd is a single wave and it arrives at noon: give the morning to the bridge, midday to the far bank and the evening to the castle, and you'll spend the whole day one step ahead of it.

itinerary.title: Ready-Made Routes
itinerary.intro: If you hate planning, follow these flows. The times are flexible; keep the spirit, break the order.

plans.title: If You Have 1 Day
plans.subtitle: A day of romance from bridge to castle

steps.title: The Alte Brücke morning
steps.description: Touch the monkey while the bridge is empty, photograph the misty river and the castle in first light; breakfast at a square bakery.

steps.title: The old town and the Karzer
steps.description: University square, the scribbled cells of the Studentenkarzer and the Heiliggeistkirche: gather the student city's soul.

steps.title: A tavern lunch
steps.description: Schnitzel or Käsespätzle in a side-lane tavern, with Palatinate wine or cask beer: Gemütlichkeit, lesson one.

steps.title: The castle and the Königstuhl
steps.description: Up by Bergbahn: courtyard, the Great Tun, the pharmacy museum and the terrace view; continue in the wooden carriage to the summit and see the valley from above.

steps.title: Sunset on the Philosophers' Way
steps.description: Cross the bridge and climb the snaking Schlangenweg stair to the path: take the best bench as the castle turns to embers in the evening light.

steps.title: Evening in the Altstadt
steps.description: Dinner at a historic tavern, then a close in the student bars of the Untere Straße: the town is small, the night warm.

plans.title: If You Have 3 Days
plans.subtitle: Live the romance layer by layer

steps.title: Classic Heidelberg
steps.description: The one-day flow above: bridge, Karzer, castle, Philosophers' Way.

steps.title: Hills and river
steps.description: A morning forest walk to the Thingstätte and the Heiligenberg monastery ruins; a Neckarwiese picnic or a river boat tour in the afternoon; neighbourhood life in Neuenheim's cafés in the evening.

steps.title: Vineyards and surroundings
steps.description: Handschuhsheim's village fabric and vineyard taverns; an afternoon train escape to Speyer cathedral or Schwetzingen palace; farewell with a box of Studentenkuss on return.

phrases.title: 5-Word Survival Kit
phrases.intro: In a university town English opens every door, but these five German words guarantee the smile.

items.meaning: Hello / good day — the second formal, the first friendly
Thank you very much — answered with 'bitte'
Please / you're welcome / here you go — German's multipurpose magic word
Cheers! — eye contact as the glasses clink is mandatory
'Warm, cosy, pleasant' — a tavern evening in one word

checklist.completion_message: Prost! You've done the capital of romance properly!
